digest.lead: Anthropic is restricting third-party harnesses like OpenClaw for Claude Code subscriptions, sparking significant community backlash with nearly 500 comments on Hacker News.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, Claude Code v2.1.92 shipped with new enterprise features and Bedrock integration, while Claude helped uncover critical RCE vulnerabilities in popular text editors.

stories.headline: Anthropic Restricts Third-Party Harnesses for Claude Subscriptions
stories.summary: Anthropic announced it will no longer allow Claude Code subscriptions to use third-party harnesses like OpenClaw [1][2]. The policy change has generated significant community discussion, with one Hacker News thread attracting nearly 500 comments expressing concern about the restriction [2].
key_points: OpenClaw and similar third-party tools will be blocked for subscription users
Community reaction has been largely negative, with extensive discussion on Hacker News
stories.perspectives: While Anthropic hasn't publicly detailed the reasoning, the restriction appears to limit how users can interface with Claude through alternative clients and tools.
stories.impact: This affects developers and power users who rely on third-party interfaces for Claude integration, potentially forcing workflow changes or subscription cancellations.

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.92 Adds Enterprise Policy Controls and Bedrock Integration
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code release introduces enterprise-focused features including a `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` policy setting for managed environments and an interactive Bedrock setup wizard [1]. The update also enhances cost tracking with per-model and cache-hit breakdowns for subscription users [1].
key_points: New fail-closed policy setting ensures fresh remote settings or blocks startup
Interactive AWS Bedrock wizard guides through authentication and configuration
Enhanced cost tracking shows detailed per-model and cache usage breakdowns
stories.impact: Enterprise teams gain better control over Claude Code deployments, while AWS users get streamlined setup and all subscription users receive improved cost visibility.

stories.headline: Claude Discovers Critical RCE Vulnerabilities in Vim and Emacs
stories.summary: Claude AI helped security researchers identify remote code execution vulnerabilities in both Vim and Emacs text editors that can be triggered simply by opening malicious files [1]. The discovery highlights AI's growing role in automated vulnerability research and code security analysis.
stories.impact: This affects millions of developers using these popular editors and demonstrates Claude's capability for security research, potentially encouraging more AI-assisted vulnerability hunting.

sources.title: Claude AI finds Vim, Emacs RCE bugs that trigger on file open

stories.headline: Travel Hacking Toolkit Uses AI for Points Optimization and Trip Planning
stories.summary: A new open-source project called Travel Hacking Toolkit leverages AI to help users search for award travel opportunities and plan trips using loyalty points [1]. The project has gained attention on Hacker News with 60 points and active community discussion.
stories.impact: This showcases practical AI applications for personal finance and travel planning, demonstrating how Claude and similar models can be integrated into specialized consumer tools.

stories.headline: Use forceRemoteSettingsRefresh policy to ensure fresh configuration on startup
stories.summary: This setting forces Claude Code CLI to fetch the latest remote managed settings before starting and exits if the fetch fails. This ensures your CLI always runs with the most current configuration and prevents running with stale settings that might cause issues.
actionable_steps: Open your Claude Code CLI configuration
Restart the CLI to verify it blocks startup until fresh settings are fetched

stories.headline: Enable PowerShell tool for Windows development workflows
stories.summary: Claude Code now includes an opt-in PowerShell tool that allows Windows users to execute PowerShell commands directly through Claude. This provides native Windows command-line access for system administration and development tasks.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.84 or later
Enable the PowerShell tool in your settings as a preview feature

stories.headline: Use @-mentions to give Claude Code precise file context
stories.summary: Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code, recommends using @-mentions to point Claude at specific files instead of letting it search. This dramatically reduces token usage and improves accuracy since Claude works with the exact files you intend rather than guessing from project structure.
actionable_steps: Type @ in Claude Code to see a file picker with fuzzy search
Select the specific files relevant to your task before writing your prompt
Combine multiple @-mentions for cross-file tasks like refactoring

stories.headline: Use environment variables to configure MCP server settings in Claude Code
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.85 introduced CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME and CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variables for MCP headersHelper scripts. This allows a single helper script to serve multiple MCP servers, simplifying configuration management.
actionable_steps: Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME environment variable to your desired server name
Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variable to your MCP server URL
Update your MCP headersHelper scripts to use these variables instead of hardcoded values

stories.headline: Configure streaming timeout for better connection handling
stories.summary: The new CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable lets you customize how long Claude Code waits before timing out idle streaming connections. This helps prevent unnecessary disconnections during long-running operations.
actionable_steps: Choose a timeout value in milliseconds (default is 90000 for 90 seconds)
Restart Claude Code for the setting to take effect
